blocks.text: Fraserview New Westminster Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Fraserview is the south slope above the North Arm of the Fraser River, and it is a board sub-area name, not one of the ten neighbourhoods on the City's Official Community Plan (OCP) residential neighbourhoods map.

The slope runs along Stewardson Way and the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) at its base, with Jamieson Court, Ross Drive and Francis Way carrying the strata stock above it, per the City's consolidated land use designations map.

The City publishes no historic neighbourhood context statement for Fraserview: its heritage context statement list covers Brow of the Hill, Connaught Heights, Downtown, Glenbrooke North, Massey-Victory Heights, McBride-Sapperton and the West End, not Fraserview.

blocks.text: Fraserview New Westminster Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The waterfront edge holds the low-rise stock: Palace Quay at 69 and 71 Jamieson Court is the largest index building on the court, with Jamieson Place townhouses at 72 Jamieson Court beside it.

Two index entries sit off the hill — Queen's Park Place at 55 Blackberry Drive and Fraserview Park at 74 Miner Street — and the counted townhouse stock is thin (245 Francis Way, 72 Jamieson Court), because most Fraserview strata are apartment-form.

blocks.text: Fraserview New Westminster Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Ground-oriented additions on this slope are design-controlled: OCP Development Permit Area (DPA) 1.2, Ground Oriented Housing, and DPA 1.3, Townhouses and Rowhouses, set the guidelines infill townhouse and rowhouse work must follow.

The foreshore itself is a protected designation: the OCP land use map carries an Intertidal designation for the Fraser River foreshore, to preserve it in a predominantly natural state, with lookouts, trails and docks as complementary uses.
Every Fraserview strata of five or more lots must hold a depreciation report on the provincial five-year cycle in force since July 1, 2024, with no deferral vote.

blocks.text: Fraserview New Westminster Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Lookout Greenspace at Mayes Street and Stewardson Way is named for its vantage point over the North Arm of the Fraser River, with trees, lawns, paths, picnic tables and benches.
The Grove at Victoria Hill is a phase, not one building: index listings place it at 250, 265, 270 and 275 Ross Drive and Francis Way.
Fraser Mews at 340, 365 and 385 Ginger Drive is filed as townhouse in some listings but is a four-storey elevator apartment building in built form, and the index counts it as an apartment.
The Lookout's commonly quoted 295 Francis Way address is its sales centre; the buildings stand at 22 East Royal Avenue.
Palace Quay carries two civic addresses, 69 and 71 Jamieson Court, for one building.

blocks.text: Fraserview New Westminster Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The 2026 home owner grant threshold on the City's page is $2,075,000 of assessed value, with the basic grant up to $570 and the additional grant up to $845, claimed from the Province rather than at City Hall, 511 Royal Avenue.
There was no 2026 property tax sale in New Westminster: the City posted on September 24, 2026 that all delinquent property taxes had been collected.

blocks.text: Fraserview New Westminster Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Route 103 is the waterfront bus: it links the Jamieson Court and Quayside streets to New Westminster Station, per TransLink's Burnaby and New Westminster schedule book.

Stewardson Way is the slope's arterial: it carries traffic between the Queensborough Bridge interchange and downtown along the base of the Fraserview hill, below the Ross Drive and Francis Way buildings.

blocks.text: Fraserview New Westminster Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start at the river: the OCP's Intertidal designation and the City's floodplain figures mean a Jamieson Court ground-floor unit needs its flood construction level and strata insurance terms checked, not assumed from the hill above it.

Check the phase, not the project name, at Victoria Hill: buildings sharing the Boiler House amenity centre and the Victoria Hill name are separate stratas on Ross Drive, Francis Way and East Royal Avenue, with separate depreciation reports.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Fraserview
One of New Westminster’s lesser-known pockets, Fraserview sits by the river. Buyers weigh the river frontage and views against the Stewardson Way and bridge traffic beside it.
Fraserview home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

71 condos sold in Fraserview with a median price of $645,000 (the middle half sold between $581,000 and $697,500), taking a median of 21 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $599 per square foot, a median year built of 2007 and a median strata fee of $580 a month. 22 townhomes sold in Fraserview with a median price of $1,077,000 (the middle half sold between $968,000 and $1,129,250), taking a median of 10 days to sell at 98.5% of the last list price; 14% sold above list. They had a median $460 per square foot, a median year built of 1994 and a median strata fee of $596 a month.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Fraserview?
faq.a: 57, in the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® month-end figures for October 2026. Listings change every day; Jared can tell you what is available now.

faq.q: Is Fraserview a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Fraserview had a sales ratio of 12%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Fraserview from June to October 2026?
faq.a: Between June and October 2026, 44 condos and townhomes sold in Fraserview; New Westminster as a whole recorded 327.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Fraserview sell for?
faq.a: 71 condos sold in Fraserview from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, at a median price of $645,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Fraserview?
faq.a: Half sold in 21 days or less, at a median 97.1% of the last list price; 6% went over asking (sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
